newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices extend gains, limited supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices extend gains, limited supply.

text.p: Indian sugar prices on Wednesday extended gains on limited supplies and a shortage of ready stock, dealers said.
In ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 8/10 rupees at 1,270/1,310 rupees per quintal while M-30 moved up by 10 rupees at 1,315/1,390 rupees.

"Arrivals remained slow in the market as traders were lifting limited quantities from the mills ahead of an indefinite strike called by transport operators," said Shantilal Dedhiya, secretary of the Bombay Sugar Merchant Association.
Indian transporters have threatened to strike from next month to protest against the imposition of service taxes and raising insurance premiums.
"Millers are facing a glut due to limited lifting by the trade and in turn sugar mill delivery dropped today to 1,170/1,180 rupees per quintal from 1,190/1,210 rupees," Dedhiya said.
Overall market sentiment at the close remained firm.
